chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdul Hameed ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, He marks in his heart a spot of light in his heart, so his hearing and his heart are illuminated by it, until he becomes more eager for what is in your hands (Al-Wilayah) than you are; and when He intends evil for a servant, He marks a black spot in his heart, so his hearing and his heart are darkened by it.
So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to make err, He makes his chest straitened and narrow as though he were ascending to the sky.
ai.seo_question: How does divine guidance manifest physically and spiritually in the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical mechanism of divine favor (Tawfiq) and misguidance (Tadlil) through the imagery of light and darkness imprinting upon the heart, a concept central to Shia gnosis (Irfan). It explicitly links this internal spiritual state to Quran 6:125, illustrating how God's will manifests as either an expanded, receptive chest for Islam or a constricted, struggling one for those destined for error. The narration underscores that true insight is a divine gift, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on God's sovereign choice in guiding the hearts of His servants.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Hameed Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, when He<sup>azwj</sup> intends goodness with a servant, Imprints a spot of Noor (light) in his heart, so it illuminates his hearing and his heart for him to the extent that he becomes greedy upon what is in your hands (Al-Wilayah) among you; and when He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends evil with a servant, Imprints a black spot in his heart, so it darkens his hearing and his heart to it’.
Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> recited this Verse

[6:125] Therefore (for) whomsoever Allah Intends that He would Guide him aright, He Expands his chest for Islam, and (for) whomsoever He Intends that He should Let him to err, He makes his chest straitened and narrow as though he were ascending to the sky’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al- Hamid ibn abu al-‘Ala’ from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, wills good for a servant. He places a dot of light in his heart, which shines his ears and heart to the extent that he becomes more eager and protective of this cause than you are. When He wills evil for a servant. He places a black dot in his heart and it darkens his ears and his heart.
Allah will open the hearts of whomever He wants to guide to Islam, but He will constrict the chest of one whom He has led astray, as though he were to climb high up into the sky. . . .’” [6:125]
